title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_0LA0RE_1RD0RA_1LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The head sweeps the whole tape. Its background is the period-3 word 100, written in three phases; the phases change at walls, and the walls come in groups of three domains of nearly equal length, separated by 000. The leftward sweeps over the domains are proved shift rules, but how the walls move between sweeps has not been made into a rule. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide, and proves the shift rules of the sweeps (lean/Rules.lean); the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,168 cells have been visited and 20,324 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.241).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: The leftward sweep, entered in each of its three phases: L (100)^n A>1 R, L (001)^n B>0 R, L (010)^n C>0 R cross a whole domain at once, turning 100 into 110, 001 into 101 and 010 into 011, for every n and all tapes L, R.

claims.title: Groups of three domains, a shrinking staircase
claims.text: Read at the right end at step 1,925,758,219 (width 50,930) the tape is 96 groups (100)^a (010)^b (001)^c separated by 000, with a, b, c within a few of each other in each group and decreasing from about 115 in the leftmost groups to about 5 at the right end, by about 2 per group with plateaus. Seen at every right-end turn of the run; not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs C to read a 1 with another 1 to its left (1 C>1, then F reads the 1). In the background the sweeps never produce that; it would have to arise at a wall. Nobody has described how the walls move from one sweep to the next, so there is no rule to iterate.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The head runs back and forth over a tape that repeats the three cells 100, but the repetition slips by one cell at walls, and the walls come in a regular staircase of groups. How the staircase evolves has not been worked out.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 37,168 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).
Groups of three domains at step 1.9·10<sup>9</sup>, sizes from about 115 down to 5.

sections.heading: A period-3 background in three phases
html: After a sweep to the right the tape repeats 100; a sweep to the left turns each triple into 110 (and the shifted copies 001, 010 into 101, 011). These leftward sweeps are proved shift rules (lean/Rules.lean). The phase of the repetition slips at walls 000. The right end of the tape at step 1,925,758,219:
and the same tape after the next sweep to the left, in the left-sweep form:

sections.heading: A staircase of groups
html: Each group between two walls holds three domains, one in each phase, of nearly the same length. Listing the lengths (a, b, c) of the 96 groups from the left at the same step gives a staircase:

The lengths fall by about 2 per group, with plateaus of equal groups. Earlier in the run the steps of the staircase were larger (domain lengths 206, 194, 182, 170, ... at step 2.2·108). This looks like a counter whose digits are the group sizes, but its carry rule has not been found.

sections.heading: One pattern at a wall
html: The machine halts on F1, reached as 1 C>1: C reads a 1 and moves left onto another 1. Inside a domain the sweeps never do that, so a halt would have to come from a wall meeting another wall or the end of the tape in an unusual phase. Without a rule for the walls this is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.241).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,168 cells (26,406 left of the start, 548 right), with a density of 1s of 0.547.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A bouncer over the period-3 background 100 whose tape is split by walls 000 into groups of three domains (100)^a (010)^b (001)^c with a ≈ b ≈ c; the group sizes form a staircase that shrinks toward one end, and the walls drift: a counter-like shape with no known rule.
family: period-3 bouncer with walls, staircase of domain groups
